rgb: The camera wearer looks downward at a woven rope cot (charpai) where they are seated, with a flat concrete or earth floor extending beyond the cot's wooden side rail about 3 to 5 metres in front of them. To the left of the wearer on the same cot, about 3 to 5 metres away, another person's striped-sleeved arm and hand are partially visible at the bottom-left frame edge, reaching toward papers and fabric beside the wearer's left elbow. Just beyond the cot's front-left rail, about 0.4 to 0.8 metres away and within reach, the dark-trousered legs and sandal-clad foot of a third person seated on or near the floor are partially visible at the upper-left edge, while a bristle broom lies on the floor to the right about 3 to 5 metres ahead. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's head turns slightly leftward and upward—shifting the cot rail from a steep diagonal to nearly horizontal and bringing more of the floor, the broom, and the two people on the left into view—while the wearer's left hand lowers slightly onto the knitted fabric.
depth: The monocular depth map captures a steep downward egocentric viewpoint over a woven bamboo-framed cot (~3–5 m below the camera) and the flat floor beyond it (~0.4–0.8 m away), showing the camera wearer's pink-draped lap and folded left arm as the brightest, farthest surfaces at ~3–5 m. Far outside the wearer's arm's reach (~3–5 m) are a mint-green knitted piece with needles on the right and a yarn ball in the center, while a white cloth, purple fabric, and a second person's striped right arm and hand sit slightly higher and nearer to the left on the cot (~0.4–0.8 m from the wearer, within reach beside the wearer's elbow). Beyond the cot's front-left bamboo rail and above the dark floor plane, a third person's crossed legs and feet in sandals appear in darker grey tones at ~0.3–0.6 m (within reach on the cot-edge side of the second person), with all three people's heads out of view so no gaze away from the wearer is visible, and body orientations indicated only by limbs facing roughly backward or diagonally toward the cot. Across frames 1 to 2, the camera turns and pitches slightly leftward as the wearer's left hand approaches the knitted fabric on the right from its resting position across their chest through frame 5, bringing the two people on the left further into the frame while the broom on the floor (~3–5 m away) shifts upward and right. Compared to RGB, the depth map much more clearly separates the elevated cot plane and the wearer's elevated forearm from the recessed floor and resolves the 3D relief of the yarn ball and fine knitting needles, though it is unreliable on the floor where the broom disappears into uniform darkness and in frame 1 where the cot's bamboo rail and rope weave are flattened into a single smooth ramp.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map attempts to parse the downward-looking scene into discrete 'person' masks against an unlabelled black background, primarily isolating the camera wearer's torso, pink garment, and left arm in the lower-center foreground (~3–5 m from the camera, far outside immediate self-reach). From frame 2 onward, separate masks at the lower-left and upper-left edges mark the partly occluded person sitting beside the wearer on the cot (~3–5 m away, out of arm's reach of the wearer and the white cloth) and the third person seated on the floor beyond the front-left cot rail (~0.4–0.8 m away, within reach of the cot edge, holding a plastic bag outside their own reach in frame 5). As the camera pans slightly leftward after frame 1 and the wearer's left arm moves from the right-side knitting to rest horizontally across their torso in frames 2–5, the left-side person masks expand into view, though all heads remain outside the frame and no one is seen looking away from the camera wearer. While the segmentation masks help distinguish the boundary between the wearer's left shoulder and the adjacent person's arm on the lower left where colorful fabrics visually merge in the RGB image, the map omits all non-person objects including the yarn, knitting needles, cloths, cot, and broom. Furthermore, the segmentation is highly unreliable across frames: it leaves a hollow gap inside the wearer's bent left arm, swaps instance colors between frames, and falsely labels the bamboo cot rail, woven ropes, white cloth, and floor broom as 'person' regions in frames 1, 3, and 5.
pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, detecting no skeletons in frame 1 and only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in frames 2 through 5 at roughly 3–5 m in front of and below the camera. Across frames 2 to 5, this magenta hand remains stationary on the right side of the wearer's chest—out of reach of the distant yarn ball (~3–5 m away) and knitted fabric to the right—after having approached the right edge of the frame between frames 1 and 2 as the camera shifted slightly leftward. In frame 5 only, a yellow body-and-face keypoint skeleton appears on the left side, spanning from the cot surface (~3–5 m away) toward the upper-left floor (~0.4–0.8 m away), while the rest of the scene—including the wearer's torso, the cot, the yarn, and the broom on the floor—remains completely unrendered. This sparse skeleton view isolates the exact finger articulation and rightward orientation of the wearer's resting left hand free from the visual clutter of the pink clothing and green wool in RGB. However, the map is largely unreliable for scene-wide spatial understanding because it misses the wearer's hand in frame 1, fails to detect the adjacent person's hand or the floor-seated person's legs and hands in frames 1–4, and in frame 5 hallucinates a single distorted yellow torso-and-head skeleton across the white cloth and adjacent arms where no head is present in the field of view.
